description: Find job postings and check whether a posting is still open. Use it to: find jobs by role and place (query, with location, remote or posted_within_days); read one posting by url and tell whether it is still open; check up to 10 posting urls in one call; list a company's open roles from its own job board (company, a name or domain; add query for one role there); and see who is hiring for a role (query with group_by "employer"). Every row has the same normalized fields: title, company, location, remote, posted_at as the board states it, url, source, a status, and checked_at, the time Firecrawl read it. status is open when the posting was read from the employer's board or live posting page in this call, and unverified when it comes from a job site and was not confirmed on the employer's board. A posting checked by url can also be closed, not_found or error. A single url returns the full description; list rows carry it with include_description. A company search names the boards it read and what each covers; when no board is found, rows come from job sites and notes says so. boards_only searches employers' own boards only. Each provider read is charged its listed price; max_credits caps the call. Example: {"query":"data engineer","location":"Berlin","posted_within_days":14}.

boards_only.description: true searches employers' own job boards only; every row is confirmed open on its board.

company.description: Company name or domain, e.g. "example.com". Lists that company's open roles from its own job board.

cursor.description: next_cursor from an earlier call with the same input, for more rows.

group_by.description: "employer" groups the postings found by employer, to see who is hiring for a role.

include_description.description: true adds the description to each list row. A single url always returns it.

limit.description: Rows wanted from a search by query or company, 1 to 100, default 10. Leave it out with url or urls.

location.description: City, region or country, e.g. "Berlin" or "Canada".

max_credits.description: Most credits the call may spend. Set it only to a budget the user gave; left out, it is 200. A provider that could pass it is not started.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

posted_within_days.description: Only postings the board dates within this many days, 1 to 365.

provider.description: Ask only this provider, e.g. "indeed". Leave it out to let Firecrawl choose.

query.description: Job title or keywords, e.g. "data engineer". With company, the role to look for there.

url.description: One posting URL to read in full and check: whether it is still open, with its description.

urls.description: Up to 10 posting URLs to check in one call; each comes back with its status.

name: jobs_search
